Quick summary from infra:
- Observed a rapid shrink in available GPUs in eu-west-dedicated-3 between 20:45–21:10 UTC due to a combination of host preempts and a backfilled batch job mis-scheduling (we're still tracing root cause).
- Autoscaler initiated scale-up at 20:46 UTC but several bootstrap images stalled; effective capacity only returned at ~21:20 UTC. During that window some routes hit accept queue timeouts producing 502/504 and our fronting layer returned 429s when request queueing exceeded limits.
- Trace: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/OSR-2347 (collected). Attached pool metrics snapshot.

Immediate recommendations (short term):
1) Failover traffic for Osiris to eu-hosted-1 for the next 2 hours (cold warm pool) — will reduce latency but slightly higher cost.
2) Apply per-route burst-limit 40r/s (from current 120r/s) for 15 minutes to damp retries while we heal pool.
3) Roll a smaller quantized variant (gpt-small-q4) as a temporary fallback for non-critical routes.

I will push the scale-up fixes and follow up with logs for the bootstrap failure.

Karthik
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer (oncall)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Action plan and exec summary — Osiris incident (eu-west)

Claire — quick executive summary and next steps:

What happened:
- Between 20:45–21:20 UTC yesterday we had a transient GPU capacity exhaustion in your eu-west dedicated pool. The autoscaler attempted to add capacity but several new nodes failed to bootstrap quickly, which created queueing that translated into 502/504 responses and 429s when the fronting layer started rejecting excess requests. Our metrics show a short retry amplification from client retries compounding the load.

What we are doing right now (live):
- We will route your critical inference route to eu-hosted-1 immediately (expected cutover < 5 minutes).
- We will deploy a quantized fallback (gpt-small-q4) and apply a conservative 40r/s burst limit to damp retries.
- Our infra team is rolling the bootstrap fix; we expect eu-west-dedicated-3 capacity to be healthy in ~60–90 minutes after the fix.

Customer impact and mitigations:
- You should see error rates fall to baseline within 6 minutes of the routing change. Latency on the hosted pool will be marginally higher (~+50–120ms).
- If you prefer no change to routing, we can instead implement per-client throttles and return a clear Retry-After header; however, that will extend recovery.

Permissions requested:
- Can we flip routing to eu-hosted-1 now and enable the q4 fallback?
- We will also propose a one-time service credit for the affected window — Marcus, will confirm amount.

I’ll update you with metrics when the routing is complete and again at 30/90 minutes. Apologies for the interruption — we’ll follow up with a post-incident summary and remediation plan later today.

— Jordan Blake
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
